transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-21
Start: 14:00 UTC
Duration: ~50 minutes
Attendees: Sophie Chen (Redwood AE), Raj Patel (Redwood SE), Lena Morozov (Northhaven Head of Platform), Daniel Park (CTO), Marta Ruiz (Security), Owen Li (SRE)

[00:00] Sophie Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick check in — happy friday, uh, we'll run through where you're at with the EU rollout and the retainer uplift ask.
[00:15] Lena Morozov: Thanks Sophie. yes, wanted to make sure we leave with timeline and cost. we've got exec alignment to move to a higher retainer but need EU privacy and KMS in place before we sign.
[00:28] Daniel Park: hi team, main thing is latency — our user flows in the EU need p95 under 180ms for short-form generation. currently we see about 220-260ms from the hosted endpoints.
[00:40] Raj Patel: okay that's helpful context. are those numbers from live production or staging? and what's the typical sequence length?
[00:50] Owen Li: production, mostly 32-64 tokens on average, some long ones up to 512 for report generation but infrequent. throughput is about 30 reqs/s average, spikes to 150 during batch hours.
[01:05] Raj Patel: got it. we suspect the p95 is being driven by cold start and KV working set evictions. If you move to dedicated pools in eu-central, we can pin warm instances and tune batching.
[01:20] Lena Morozov: can you explain the dedicated option again? cost looks steeper but maybe worth it for latency.
[01:28] Sophie Chen: yes so dedicated here means reserved GPU capacity just for Northhaven. predictable throughput, you get autoscaling config and reserved slot capacity — less noisy neighbor variance. Pricing is a monthly commit. we provided a ballpark earlier (see spreadsheet link: https://redwood.internal/pricing/northhaven-eu).
[01:45] Marta Ruiz: security question — for a dedicated pool in our VPC, how is key management handled? we need customer-managed keys, and audit logs forwarded to our SIEM.
[01:55] Raj Patel: we support KMS/HSM integrations — you can provide an external KMS or use our managed KMS with customer key wrap. audit logs are exportable; we push near-real-time events to your logging endpoint via secure pipeline. i'll share the integration doc.
[02:12] Marta Ruiz: and SOC2 evidence? we need a timeline for attestation and the scope includes network segregation.
[02:20] Sophie Chen: yes, SOC2 report is in our security pack — i'll re-share the attestation and we can do a focused Q&A. timeline: we can give you current report immediately, and for anything new specific to your VPC we can map controls; expect a 2-3 week Q&A cycle.
[02:35] Daniel Park: What about data residency — will data ever leave eu-central? we have to guarantee no egress to us-west.
[02:45] Raj Patel: with a private/VPC deployment we can constrain routing to eu regions only. there is a control plane but the private option gives you a customer-controlled control plane — minimal metadata may route to our control plane in region but payloads stay in region. we should detail that in the architecture note.
[03:05] Lena Morozov: timeline wise, if we approve the uplift next tuesday, when can eu dedicated pool be provisioned?
[03:12] Sophie Chen: typical provisioning for dedicated eu cluster is 4-6 weeks after contract signature and capacity commit, shorter if we can reuse pre-warmed GPUs in our pool — could be as fast as 3 weeks but we should plan 6 to be safe.
[03:25] Owen Li: we might run a pilot first — a week or two of perf testing before full cutover. can Redwood support a dedicated pilot?
[03:33] Raj Patel: absolutely. we can stand up a pilot cluster with limited capacity and run the perf harness. that's what we're proposing for the upcoming perf test.
[03:45] Lena Morozov: on cost — i saw a 30% delta between hosted with committed bursts and dedicated. can you show impact per 10M tokens?
[03:55] Sophie Chen: yes, that's in the sheet. high level: hosted w/ burst is cheapest at low sustained throughput, dedicated gives better unit cost at scale because of predictable batching and KV cache locality. i'll calculate a side-by-side for your monthly profile.
[04:12] Marta Ruiz: any callouts on encryption in flight and at rest? we need TLS, enforced cipher suites, and full-disk encryption on the nodes.
[04:20] Raj Patel: TLS for all ingress/egress. nodes are encrypted at rest and we can attach customer-managed keys for disk encryption. i'll put the exact cypher suite and configuration in the security appendix.
[04:35] Daniel Park: about fallbacks — what happens if dedicated capacity saturates? auto-fallback to hosted? This is critical for our SLAs.
[04:45] Sophie Chen: yes we support automatic fallback policies — requests can route to compatible hosted variants. you control the policy (latency-first or cost-first) and can set throttles. we'll show you the route policy config in the console.
[05:00] Owen Li: i want to call out egress and egress charges for EU to where our data lake sits — we likely keep logs in eu but replicate analytics to us-west, what's typical?
[05:12] Raj Patel: we advise keeping tokens and PII in-region, streaming non-sensitive metrics cross-region if needed; we can gate replication by dataset. egress fees follow cloud provider rules; we can model monthly estimates once you give us expected volume.
[05:28] Lena Morozov: okay, security gating is the blocker. Marta will send list of artefacts and we'll need to confirm SOC2 coverage.
[05:35] Marta Ruiz: yes i'll send the artefact list. also, SSO — we use Okta, and we need SAML 2.0 and SCIM for provisioning.
[05:45] Raj Patel: Okta SAML + SCIM are supported; we can do RBAC mapping and provisioning. we'll include a sample metadata file and attribute mapping.
[06:00] Sophie Chen: recap — action items: Sophie to share updated pricing and commitment tiers; Raj to schedule perf test; Marta to share audit artefact list. Any other blockers?
[06:10] Daniel Park: timeline: we aim to sign week of 2026-03-29 after perf test.
[06:18] Sophie Chen: great, we'll get the perf test scheduled for the week of 2026-03-28. we'll share the test plan and the workload files ahead of time.
[06:25] Lena Morozov: can you include a 'failover playbook' example in that plan — we want to see failover timings and metrics.
[06:32] Raj Patel: yes, we'll include failover playbook, typical RTO/RPO numbers and what triggers fallback to hosted.
[06:40] Owen Li: small note — our SREs want to test KV-cache stress; can you model eviction behavior under mixed workloads?
[06:48] Raj Patel: we'll include that in the perf harness: mixed traffic, long seq bursts, KV cache thrash scenarios.
[06:55] Sophie Chen: ok wrapping up, i'll send the updated pricing doc and SOC2 pack, raj will follow up with scheduling. thanks everyone.

End of transcript.

References shared during call:
- Pricing spreadsheet: https://redwood.internal/pricing/northhaven-eu (referenced)
- Security pack: https://redwood.internal/security/soc2-pack (Sophie to resend)
- Perf test plan placeholder: https://redwood.internal/perf/northhaven/pilot-proposal (Raj to populate)

Recap (quick bullet):
- Northhaven intends to uplift retainer post perf test; target sign week of 2026-03-29.
- Redwood to run pilot/perf test week of 2026-03-28 focusing on p95 latency and KV cache scenarios.
- Security gating: Marta to provide required artefacts; Redwood to provide SOC2 attestation & KMS integration details.
- Next meeting: perf test readout (scheduled after test), Sophie to coordinate calendar.
